aboutTitle: Making urban knowledge a shared resource.
aboutText: TOSCA is the Toolkit for Open and Sustainable City Planning and Analysis. Initiated through cooperation between Digital City Science at HafenCity University Hamburg and GIZ in 2019, it brings web-based geographic information tools into collaborative planning.
aboutSecond: Its development connects research with practical applications: affordable housing, disaster preparedness, participatory land-use planning, public health, and urban mobility.
contactText: TOSCA brings researchers, public institutions, and local partners together. Contact Digital City Science at HafenCity University Hamburg to discuss research and collaboration.

currentText: TOSCA continues to develop within SUMO_15, part of Next Generation City Networking (NGCN).
featuresIntro: From shared geographic knowledge to participation and connected urban applications.
platformStory: The India projects marked a stronger technical focus: refactoring TOSCA into a cloud-ready, no-code platform. New ideas and real-world use cases continue to shape that foundation.
timeline1Text: TOSCA began with planning ideas, theoretical foundations, and local use cases. The early pilots explored how geographic information could support shared urban decisions.
timeline2Text: New contexts brought new planning questions. Local collaborations continued to develop the ideas and use cases behind the toolkit.
timeline3Text: Across the TOSCA India projects, we refactored the platform to become cloud-ready and no-code. Technical development gained a stronger focus, while research, planning ideas, and practical use cases continued alongside it.
timeline4Text: SUMO_15 / NGCN carries platform development forward, connecting the technical foundation with new urban questions and applications.
featureGisText: Bring geographic information together in the browser to explore places and support collaborative planning.
featureStoryText: Combine maps and narratives to communicate urban knowledge and explain places in context.
featureEventText: Organize and explore place-based events as part of a shared picture of the city.
featureFeedbackText: Collect feedback and bring local perspectives into discussions about places and planning.
feature3dText: Explore and interact with three-dimensional urban environments. This capability is planned for further development.
featureSimulationText: Connect urban simulations with the platform to explore scenarios and potential changes. Integrations are part of the upcoming direction.
